extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office personnel and patent practitioners/third‑party filers (patent owners, third‑party requesters)
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte reexamination & prior art citation
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for citing patents/printed publications in patent files and for filing/processing ex parte reexamination requests in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Includes content, timing, service, processing, decision criteria, forms, and certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for citation of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office in writing prior art consisting of patents or printed publications which that person believes to have a bearing on the patentability of any claim of a particular patent (35 U.S.C. 301).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The citation and an explanation of pertinency become part of the official file; at the written request of the person citing the prior art, his or her identity will be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential. See related rules and MPEP chapter for implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.501 — Requirements for citations entered in patent files
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, any person may cite prior art patents or printed publications to the Office and state them to be pertinent and applicable to the patent (37 CFR 1.501).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the citation is by the patent owner, explanation may include how claims differ from prior art. Citations shall be entered in the patent file except as set forth in §§ 1.502 and 1.902. If identity confidentiality is desired, submit without any identification. Citations should either reflect that a copy was mailed to patent owner or be filed in duplicate if service not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in a prior art citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art submitted under 35 U.S.C. 301 is limited to written prior art consisting of patents or printed publications and must include an explanation of how the submitted art is pertinent and applicable to the patent and why it bears on patentability of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum include a broad statement of pertinency/applicability to the claims (e.g., statement that art was made of record in a related application). Preferred to include copies of cited patents/publications and necessary English translations, identification of the patent (number, issue date, patentee), and cover sheet with documents firmly attached. Affidavits or declarations may accompany citations to explain contents or dates; patent owners may include affidavits of commercial success or enablement challenges tied to a cited document. A prior art citation must be directed to patents/printed publications and must not include issues not directed to such documents (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112 arguments, public use assertions, or statements about the patent owner's conduct). If such extraneous issues are present, the citation should not be entered and should be handled per MPEP §2206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of pertinency and manner of applying cited art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art citation must contain at least some broad statement of the pertinency and applicability of the art submitted to the patentability of the claims of the patent for which the citation is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reexamination requests, 37 CFR 1.510 requires a detailed explanation pointing out each substantial new question of patentability and the manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested; the requester may also point out how claims distinguish over cited art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may cite prior art / file reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: “Any person” may submit prior art citations or request ex parte reexamination — this includes individuals, corporate or governmental entities, patentees, licensees, reexamination requesters, real parties in interest, and persons without a real interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons may act for real parties in interest without identifying them. If confidentiality is desired, do not identify oneself in the papers; include an unsigned statement indicating the patent owner has been sent a copy (or provide a duplicate copy when service is not possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the identity of the citer
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person making the citation wishes his or her identity to be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential, the citation papers must be submitted without any identification of the person making the submission (37 CFR 1.501(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete assurance of exclusion cannot be guaranteed; persons desiring confidentiality are advised not to identify themselves anywhere in their papers. Confidential citations should include at least an unsigned statement indicating the patent owner has been sent a copy of the citation papers; if service on patent owner is not possible, a duplicate copy should accompany the citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing prior art citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations of prior art may be filed “at any time” during the period of enforceability of a patent (defined by rule as “any time during the period of enforceability”), which is the term of the patent plus 6 years under 35 U.S.C. 286, with certain litigation exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations submitted after the date of an order to reexamine will not be entered until the reexamination proceeding has concluded except if submitted by (A) the patent owner, (B) an ex parte reexamination requester who also submits the fee and required documents, (C) an inter partes requester with fee and documents, (D) in an ex parte third party requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.535, or (E) as an enterable submission pursuant to 37 CFR 1.948 in inter partes proceedings. To ensure prior art cited by a third party is considered without payment of another reexamination fee, it must be presented before reexamination is ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing responsibilities and Technology Center handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art citations received are forwarded to the Technology Center (TC) that examines the class/subclass of the patent; the TC must immediately determine whether a citation meets statutory and rule requirements and enter it into the patent file at the appropriate time if proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a citation is proper but filed after an order for reexamination and not entitled to entry during reexamination, it is retained in TC storage until the reexamination is concluded and an e‑tag placed in the reexamination file as reminder. Citations stored during reexamination are not considered by the examiner during that reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of citations that qualify for entry (third party before order)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper citation (limited to patents/printed publications) is filed prior to an order in any pending reexamination, it should be immediately entered into the reexamination file or placed in the patent file if no reexamination is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the citation indicates service on the patent owner, it is entered without notice to any party; if no indication of service, the patent owner should be notified that a citation has been entered and a duplicate copy sent if present. Sample notification wording is provided in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of citations filed after order (third party after order)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper citation is filed after an order for reexamination, the citation is not entered at the time because of the ongoing reexamination but is stored until conclusion of the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner and sender (if known) should be notified of storage. If duplicate copy filed, the duplicate should be sent to patent owner with notification; otherwise the original (in storage) should be made available for copying by the patent owner. Notification enables patent owner to consider submitting the art under 37 CFR 1.555 or 1.933 or third party to consider filing a separate request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling citations that do NOT qualify for entry (third party)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the citation is not proper (not limited to patents or printed publications), it should not be entered in the patent file and the sender (if known) and the patent owner should be notified that the citation is improper and is not being entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action varies: if service included and sender identity known, return originals to sender and notify patent owner; if sender identity unknown, discard originals; if no service but sender known and duplicate copy present, return originals and send duplicate to patent owner; if no service and sender unknown, send originals to patent owner. See MPEP §2206 for matrix of handling options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling citations filed by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper prior art citation is filed by the patent owner, it should be entered in the file whether filed prior to or after an order for reexamination; no notification to the patent owner is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an improper citation is filed by the patent owner prior to an order, it should not be entered and should be returned to the patent owner with notification. Patent owner submissions after an order should be entered under 37 CFR 1.555 (ex parte) or 1.933 (inter partes) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on the patent owner — address and method
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any submission of a citation of prior art patents or printed publications in a patent file should be served on the patent owner so that the patent owner is kept informed; service should be addressed to the correspondence address as set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2222 for details on correspondence address and service. If service not possible, file duplicate copy with Office and explain why service was not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination — basic characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person can request ex parte reexamination at any time during enforceability; prior art considered is limited to patents or printed publications; a substantial new question of patentability must be present; the actual reexamination proceeding is ex parte if ordered; decision on request must be made no later than 3 months from filing; proceedings proceed with special dispatch; scope and claim amendment limits apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional specifics: claims cannot be enlarged by amendment; reexamination normally conducted to conclusion and issuance of a reexamination certificate unless prosecution reopened by Director; reexamination and patent files are open to public (with electronic access via IFW/PAIR).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510 — Required content of a request for ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include: (1) a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications; (2) identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested and a detailed explanation of pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim; (3) a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon, with English translations of necessary parts of non‑English documents; (4) a copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims) and any disclaimers/certificates; (5) a certification that a copy of the request has been served on the patent owner if requester is not the owner; and (6) payment of the reexamination fee (37 CFR 1.510(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies must be plainly written on one side of sheet. If appropriate, requester may point out how claims distinguish over cited art. The Director will send a copy of the request to the owner if requester is not owner. Use of transmittal form PTO/SB/57 is available but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service for reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request filed by a person other than the patent owner must include a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the correspondence address provided in §1.33(c) (37 CFR 1.510(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must identify the name and address of the party served. Failure to certify service will affect processing; Director will send a copy to owner promptly when requester is not the owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for ex parte reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must be in writing and accompanied by payment of a reexamination fee established by the Director (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required for simple prior art citations under 37 CFR 1.501, but the reexamination request itself requires the fee. Partial refund procedures apply if reexamination is denied (see MPEP §2244 re processing concluded files and 37 CFR 1.26(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination will be ordered only if the Office determines that a 'substantial new question of patentability' is presented based on prior patents or printed publications (35 U.S.C. 303(a) and 37 CFR 1.510).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination statute was amended (e.g., 2002) to expand what qualifies as a substantial new question in specific situations; see MPEP §2242 POLICY IN SPECIFIC SITUATIONS for details. Request must point out each substantial new question and explain how cited art applies to every claim at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on reexamination scope and rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art considered during reexamination is limited to prior art patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103; certain limitations exist as to the kind of rejections which may be made in reexamination (claims cannot be broadened by amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination prosecution is similar to regular examination but with notable differences including special reexamination forms and time periods for special dispatch. See MPEP §§2254–2294 for handling during proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timelines and special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on a request for ex parte reexamination must be made no later than 3 months from its filing, and the remainder of proceedings must proceed with 'special dispatch' within the Office (35 U.S.C. 305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordered, the proceeding will normally be conducted to conclusion and issuance of a reexamination certificate; see MPEP for time reporting and special processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and public access to reexamination files
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination and patent files are open to the public; the reexamination file is scanned into IFW to provide an electronic format copy available through PAIR; paper files are not available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access and copying are to be made from the electronic copy; note specific handling for concluded files and distribution of certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must not initiate placing citations into files
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners should not, at their own initiative, place in a patent file or forward for placement any citations of prior art; examiners are responsible for making patentability decisions for the Director and initiating citations in other files outside their pending cases is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such examiner activity that appears to indicate claims are not patentable outside cases pending before them is considered inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and notification when citation is improper and by whom
rubrics_metrics.description: When a citation does not qualify for entry, the handling depends on whether it was filed by a third party or the patent owner, whether service of a copy was included, whether the sender is known, and whether duplicate copies are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If third party and improper: return original to sender and notify owner if service included and sender known; send duplicate to patent owner if present when sender identity known but no service; if sender unknown, send original to patent owner; if patent owner filed improper citation, return to patent owner with notification. Unusual problems should be brought to Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of court decisions and litigation material into patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solicitor’s Office processes notices required by 35 U.S.C. 290 from clerks of courts and enters them in the patent file; the Office will accept copies of notices of suits and court decisions for placement in the patent file provided they are submitted without additional comment and limited to the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During reexamination, submissions limited to bare notice with copies of the papers of the proceedings will be accepted and placed in the file to ensure complete file with updated status information regarding prior or concurrent proceedings; patent owner is required under certain CFRs to provide information regarding such proceedings if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and checklists to be used in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific PTO/PTOL forms must be used in ex parte reexamination actions and processing (e.g., PTOL‑471 Granting/Denying Request, PTOL‑466 Office Action in Ex Parte Reexamination, PTOL‑467 Advisory Action, PTOL‑468 Notification re Appeal, PTOL‑469 Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate, PTOL‑1516 Examiner Checklist, PTOL‑1517 Reexamination Clerk Checklist, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Request for Ex Parte Reexamination Transmittal Form PTO/SB/57 is available on the USPTO website for filing; its use is not mandatory. Examiners and clerks must complete checklists and process concluded files for certificate issuance as set forth in MPEP §2287.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination certificate format, numbering, and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reexamination proceeding is concluded with a certificate, it is titled 'Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate' with an ordinal number and a kind code suffix; it identifies the patent (and reexamination request number), lists prior art cited that were part of the reexamination file, and indicates the status of each claim (confirmed, canceled, disclaimed, not examined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New claims printed in italics; amended claims printed with italics and bracketing showing amendments. The certificate denotes issue date (INID code [45]), inventor, classification, abstract, and prior art at INID code [56] limited to documents in the reexamination file. Distribution includes e‑copy associated with patent in search files, depository libraries, and foreign offices with exchange agreements. Intervening rights consequences per 35 U.S.C. 307 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination of a reexamination — treatment of prior certificate changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request filed on a patent for which a reexamination certificate already issued is to be considered based on the patent as modified by the previously issued reexamination certificate (i.e., claims as modified by certificate are the operative claims for the new request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new reexamination file is received, TC clerk must incorporate certificate changes into the reexamination specification prior to forwarding to examiner. Examiner should review the entry to ensure all certificate changes were entered. Any amendment that merely re‑adds italicized (certificate) text already present is improper (informal) and should be handled under 37 CFR 1.530 and MPEP §2266.02. Each reexamination of a reexamination must be reviewed by a TC Special Program Examiner and a TC paralegal.
